title: Add partial index on dispatches(expires_at) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL

story.i_want_to: add a partial index on the dispatches table to speed up the RevokeExpiredDispatchesWorker query
story.so_that: the worker's 60-second scan of expired dispatches uses an index instead of a full table scan, reducing database load by a constant factor per tenant

rationale: RevokeExpiredDispatchesWorker runs every 60 seconds and queries `SELECT id, api_key_id FROM dispatches WHERE revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at < now()`. The existing index [:tenant_id, :expires_at] is not selective (many dispatches are not revoked), so the query often devolves to a table scan. A partial index (WHERE revoked_at IS NULL) filters the index itself to only non-revoked rows, allowing the query planner to use the index on a much smaller keyspace. This is a quick win: migration only, no code change.

acceptance_criteria.description: A new migration adds a partial index: CREATE INDEX dispatches_expires_at_unrevoked_idx ON dispatches(expires_at) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL
The migration is reversible (DROP INDEX IF EXISTS dispatches_expires_at_unrevoked_idx)
After migration, EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the RevokeExpiredDispatchesWorker query shows the index is used (Index Scan instead of Seq Scan)
Query latency for RevokeExpiredDispatchesWorker is reduced or stable; no regression

test_cases.name: Partial index is created and present in database
steps: Query pg_indexes for an index named dispatches_expires_at_unrevoked_idx
Verify the index definition includes WHERE revoked_at IS NULL
expected_results: Index exists and is correctly defined

test_cases.name: Index is used by the revoke worker query
preconditions: dispatches table has 1000+ rows with mixed revoked_at status
steps: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on: SELECT id, api_key_id FROM dispatches WHERE revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at < now()
expected_results: Plan includes Index Scan or Index Only Scan on dispatches_expires_at_unrevoked_idx

test_cases.name: Migration is reversible
expected_results: Forward migration can be rerun without conflict

notes: This is a low-risk change (index only, no table/code changes). It can be deployed independently and is safe to add/drop on a live system with low contention risk. If the table is very large (millions of rows) and mostly non-revoked, this index could improve the worker's latency significantly (10s to 100s of ms).
